verdictSummary: Candidate 04 substantively resolves the review-03 findings for the cases they named. The 10 closed path sites, the complete-string '..' law, owner functions that no longer raise untyped exceptions, the prepared mode law for all-fresh sets, the UNSATISFIABLE/PRECONDITION_FAILED split and the canonical send schedule are all reproduced from the 39 declared inputs (check 478/0, selftest 108/108). TS2 67108864 and the send-schedule arithmetic are independently reproduced. Four new required findings follow from independent probes. (1) A defaulted prepared set with one stale row bypasses the wire limit: 299 usable rows pass, the planner accepts, and the carrier refuses ARRAY_BOUND. (2) The ECMA evaluator successor changes consumers outside its declared parents, including identity LogicalPath via IM.C, and its 'unchanged' claim is false. (3) The relation-payload CanonicalPath keeps the defective lookahead, contradicting 'every occurrence', and still admits x<LF>/../y.rs. (4) The reference sender does not enforce its own Cancel law: it accepts a Cancel before Hello and a Cancel with a wrong echo.

requiredFindings.title: A defaulted prepared set with one stale row bypasses the wire limit, and the planner then accepts a prepared manifest the carrier refuses
evidence: Probe (scratch/probe_sender_prepared.out.json P_prepared.defaulted), successor-installed owner: 300 inert rows, rows[0] stale (toolchainDigest), explicit=false.
Owner prepared_output_set_admit returns fallback-non-prepared with 299 usableRows (owner PO-1 per-owner fallback).

prepared_output_set_admit_successor applies PREPARED-V3-WIRE-LIMIT only when owner outcome == 'admitted', so it returns fallback-non-prepared with 299 usableRows, no refusal and no wireLimitDisclosure.
The same 300 rows all fresh in defaulted mode fall back with disclosure and 0 usable rows. Adding one stale row turns the limit off.
Planner: REQ plan with 299 prepared entries returns no refusal (largest PreparedOutputManifest 295625 bytes). REQUEST-WIRE-ACCOUNTING checks frame bytes and totals only, not maxPreparedOutputEntries.

Carrier: K.frame_payload('rust-semantic','PreparedOutputManifest', 299 entries) is refused with ARRAY_BOUND. The accepted request would therefore become a host encode refusal or a worker protocol fault.
Explicit mode with the same set is correctly refused by the owner stale refusal, which takes precedence.
requiredFindings.fix: Apply the wire limit to the rows that would actually be selected under every non-rejected owner outcome, including fallback-non-prepared with usableRows, counting usable rows and their blob bytes. Decide and publish the defaulted outcome (for example fallback with 0 usable rows and wireLimitDisclosure plus the stale list). Also make the planner refuse a manifest whose entry count exceeds the declared entry bounds (maxPreparedOutputEntries, maxSnapshotEntries, maxDependencySourceEntries) as defense in depth. Add a defaulted stale-plus-over-limit vector and the 299-entry planner vector.

requiredFindings.title: The ECMA evaluator successor changes consumers outside its declared parents, and its 'unchanged' claim is false
evidence: install() replaces ExactValidator in every canonical module reachable from each model. My probe lists the patched instances: identity_canonical (twice, including IM.C), wire_canonical and startup_canonical from NE; startup_canonical from ST; wire_canonical from WI (scratch/probe_dialect_scope.out.json).

The successor parents are evidence, startup, handshake, occupancy, factBatch3, canonical, nativeModel, startupModel and wireModel. identitySchemas2/3, workflowCommon, relationRegistry2, c2v3 and rust2 are not parents.

Executed consumer change: identity-schemas.v3 #/$defs/LogicalPath validated through NE.IM.C gives 'a/..<LF>' refused under the pinned owner and admitted with the successor installed. That pattern ((^|/)\.\.?(/|$) under not) contains no terminator-bounded lookahead, so 'unchanged: every pattern without the terminator-bounded lookahead' is false.

Corpus-level Python-vs-ECMA changes in non-parent documents (35-string corpus, 0 unsupported constructs): c2v3 (4 patterns, e.g. canonicalIdentifier/semanticVersion/sha256Hex with a trailing LF), rust2 (DigestHex, Sha256Text with a trailing LF), identity v2/v3 and workflows common (LogicalPath/not on a/..<LF>), relationRegistry2 (CanonicalPath).
The scope is not pinned: my mutant m_patch_native_C_only_not_IM (patch only the native model's C, not IM.C, startup or wire copies) fails 0 of 478 checks.
requiredFindings.fix: State the exact normative scope of the evaluator law as a closed list of (schema document, consumer function or validator instance) pairs, with parents for every affected document. Either restrict installation to those instances and documents, or add identity, workflows, c2v3, rust2 and relation-registry parents with per-document consumer-impact rows (which values change, and why ECMA is the owner's selected semantics there). Correct the 'unchanged' list. Add controls in both directions: a narrowed installation must fail, and an out-of-scope consumer change must be declared or refused.

requiredFindings.title: The reference sender does not enforce its published Cancel law
evidence: HOST-SEND-SCHEDULE: 'A Cancel may take the next sequence number at most once, at any point after Hello'. P3-29 *PRE_COMPLETE is WAIT_HELLO_ACK..READY_COMPLETE and excludes START, and transitions.cancel.hostMaySendInStart=false.
sender_ref.consume accepts [Cancel] as the first frame (sequence 0, before Hello): framesSent 1, complete true.

consume accepts a Cancel with a different executionId of the same length ('exec-2026-09-13-0000' against the planned '-0001') and with analysisOrdinal 7. It compares only the measured size with the reserve, although the reserve is defined as the 'maximal echo Cancel'. A wrong reason is caught only by the carrier CONST check.

My mutant m_sender_no_payload_bytes_check (payload-byte divergence no longer refused) fails 0 checks, so the claimed 'payload-byte mismatch' refusal has no regression control. m_sender_no_request_limit_recheck also fails 0 (see A-2).
requiredFindings.fix: In consume, refuse a Cancel before the Hello slot has been consumed, and refuse a Cancel whose payload is not exactly {executionId, analysisOrdinal} of the planned request with reason user-interrupt. Add HOST-SEND-SCHEDULE vectors for cancel-before-hello, cancel-wrong-execution and cancel-wrong-ordinal, plus a same-type, same-coordinates, different-payload-bytes slot divergence.
